title: messaging.py: _next_id never updated after POST
description: Lines 137-162: The method uses `candidate_next_id` as a local variable initialized from `self._next_id`, increments it after assigning an auto-generated ID, but never writes it back to `self._next_id`. Result: every message POSTed without an explicit `id` field receives ID 1, overwriting any previous message with that ID in `_sent`. Second POST without id will silently replace the first message.
close_reason: Dup of worker6-s91u/hppr. Root cause: render_post incremented candidate_next_id but never wrote it back to self._next_id, so every auto-assigned POST reused ID 1 and overwrote the prior sent message. Fixed once in python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py:159 (self._next_id = candidate_next_id, persisted across requests for process lifetime; no await or early return between read and write, so atomic under the asyncio event loop; module spawns no threads). Verified by tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py (_next_id==2 after one auto POST; u64 saturation persists) and full messaging suite: 119 passed.
